summary: Interpreted the revised shutdown probe, whose post-shutdown phase isolates the defect from the shutdown race: of 8 VerifyLeader calls made after Shutdown() had already returned, only 4, 3 and 3 were answered (all with 'raft is already shutdown') while 4, 5 and 5 returned futures still incomplete 500ms later — 14 of 24 stranded, a per-call coin flip rather than a rare race. Barrier and Apply answered all 48 of their post-shutdown calls with the shutdown error, and the no-shutdown controls left nothing incomplete; the source explains the split, since verifyCh is buffered with 64 slots while applyCh is unbuffered by default, so only the verify send stays selectable after the loop exits. I corrected the existing Fact under its own id: the operative condition is the buffered channel plus a future without ShutdownCh, not the timing of the shutdown, with the racing form from the first receipt kept as the timing-dependent manifestation that did not reproduce in this revision (0 of 128 per case), and I added the joint-history reasoning linking the two receipts of the same harness lineage. No execution requested. Unfinished: a BatchApplyCh configuration, where the apply path should inherit the same behaviour, is still unmeasured.
